# Typography

Acuity sets body text in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next^[@AtkinsonHyperlegibleFont2019], a typeface designed by the Braille Institute for maximum legibility. Headings use EB Garamond for typographic contrast, and code is set in JetBrains Mono. All three load from Google Fonts.

# Layout & Margins

The page is a two-column grid: a body column for prose and a margin column for annotation. Figures, citations, and footnotes flow into the margin rather than interrupting the text.


Wideblock elements span both columns when a figure or table is too wide for the body alone:

::: {.wideblock}
![A wide image spanning body and margin columns.](https://placehold.co/1100x300/88CCEE/black?text=Wide+Image){#fig-wide-test}
:::

# Code

Code blocks carry a left border instead of a background fill. The border marks the block as code without enclosing it in a box that fights the page color. Inline `code` uses a faint tint of the accent color.

```{r}
#| label: fig-sin
#| column: margin
#| fig-cap: "Margin figures can include plots. This one anchors to the code section."
plot(sin, -pi, 2*pi)
```

# Color Palette

[Paul Tol's color palette](https://sronpersonalpages.nl/~pault/), designed to remain distinguishable under color-blindness, provides the named swatches. Semantic roles — primary, success, warning, danger — are mapped separately in `_brand.yml` and drive callout colors and link accents.

{{< include build/figures/palette.qmd >}}

Callouts inherit semantic colors from the palette:

::: {.callout-note}
**Info** — cyan `{{< brand color cyan >}}`
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
**Success** — green `{{< brand color green >}}`
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
**Warning** — sand `{{< brand color sand >}}`
:::

::: {.callout-important}
**Danger** — wine `{{< brand color wine >}}`
:::
